note: The original describes only the soldier; the alate is separated from C. dudleyi in the key on wing-venation characters but is not described, so this entry has no alate section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier with the pronotum no more than twice as wide as long, mandibles not visible in dorsal view; the margin of the frontal prominence vertical, the anterior margin of the pronotum with an oblique shallow notch. In the same genus, C. brevicollis has the pronotum about three times as wide as long; C. dudleyi has the mandibles visible in dorsal view, the margin of the frontal prominence sloping posteriorly, and the anterior margin of the pronotum deeply and roundly emarginate. The alate is not described; in the original key it is distinguished by the absence of oblique branches at the ends of the wing veins and by the coarsely punctate membrane.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head black anteriorly and reddish brown posteriorly; anterior margin of the pronotum brown, the rest pale. Head in dorsal view only slightly longer than wide, anterior part slightly wider than posterior, sides weakly contracted; anterior margin raised, medially concave, laterally rounded; anterior surface with faint transverse wrinkles. Head in profile about one and a quarter times as long as high. Mandibles very short, not visible in dorsal view. Pronotum about one and a quarter times as wide as long, anterior margin slightly obliquely notched, sides slightly narrowed and smoothly passing into the posterior margin. Head length 1 mm, total length 3.5 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The type specimen was collected in Panama, in wood on a window sill (collected by Beaumont); the holotype is in the American Museum of Natural History and the paratype in the Museum of Comparative Zoology.
